summary_html: The child is **removed from the home** and placed in foster care under court order or emergency authority. Federal statutes tie funding to safety findings, judicial oversight, and permanency planning.
authority_html:
- **ASFA / SSA Title IV-E** — removal, reasonable-efforts, and permanency requirements  
- **CFSR Regulations (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal monitoring of placement decisions

primary_citations.citation_text: Oklahoma - Title 10A (Children and Juvenile Code), § 1-2-101 (Duty to report) and Article 1, Part 4 (deprived child proceedings)
Title 10a: Children and Juvenile Code - CHILD WELFARE PRIMARY

provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed orders continuing visitation with a reunification goal and directing a change of foster placement, finding no abuse of discretion in the trial court's weighing of conflicting evidence about the child's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: B.T.W. confirms that a court may order DHS to move a child out of a foster home whose environment does not promote the permanency plan.
key_cases.quote: In making such decisions, the paramount consideration remains the best interests of the child.

key_cases.case_name: In the Matter of K.G. v. Department of Human Services
key_cases.court: Court of Civil Appeals of Oklahoma
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the denial of foster grandparents' objection to DHS's emergency removal of their foster child, holding that the reasonable-suspicion standard governs whether an emergency justified physically removing a child from a foster home.
key_cases.relevance: It is the leading Oklahoma decision on a foster parent's right to object to removal and the standard the agency must satisfy.
key_cases.quote: the trial court is faced with an inquiry into whether an emergency exists to justify physical removal of the child from an existing foster home, the reasonable suspicion standard applies

key_cases.court: Court of Civil Appeals of Oklahoma
key_cases.holding: The court held that placing Indian children with their mothers after emergency removal from the father was a foster care placement triggering ICWA § 1912(d), and affirmed the finding that the State made active efforts by clear and convincing evidence before adjudication.
key_cases.relevance: It defines when an out-of-home arrangement counts as a foster care placement for federal purposes even though the child lives with a parent.
key_cases.quote: We find no reason why the same case-by-case review should not be applied when deciding if State has made the required active efforts in this foster care placement.

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The Tenth Circuit held that caseworkers who entered a family's home and removed a child without a warrant, prior notice or a hearing, in the absence of exigent or extraordinary circumstances, violated the Fourth and Fourteenth Amendments, though the defendants might still establish qualified immunity on remand.
key_cases.relevance: Placement into foster care that begins with an unconstitutional entry and seizure is itself constitutionally infirm.
key_cases.quote: We find no special need that renders the warrant requirement impracticable when social workers enter a home to remove a child, absent exigent circumstances.

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The Tenth Circuit affirmed the denial of qualified immunity to a caseworker who recommended placing and keeping a child in his father's custody and failed to investigate mounting evidence that the father was abusing him, holding this violated clearly established state-created-danger law.
key_cases.relevance: Placement recommendations are affirmative acts for which a caseworker can be personally liable when they create or increase danger to the child.
key_cases.quote: Ms. Patton's conduct violated T.D.'s clearly established substantive due process right under Currier to be free from state-created danger.

key_cases.holding: In the second B.T.W. appeal the court affirmed a post-appeal permanency order that kept the child with her foster mother, limited the mother to supervised visitation and changed the permanency plan to long-term out-of-home placement, finding reasonable efforts had been made and no abuse of discretion or due process violation.
key_cases.relevance: It confirms the trial court's continuing equitable power over where a deprived child is placed and how much contact the parent gets.
key_cases.quote: A trial court's findings concerning visitation and placement of a child previously adjudicated as deprived are matters of equitable cognizance.

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives
